newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Copper may test $2,366 resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Copper may test $2,366 resistance.

text.p: 3 MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
Copper prices could attempt the important resistance at $2,366 a tonne on Friday having achieved a bullish close the previous night, technical analysts said.
Aluminium prices looked like consolidating after their recent break, before trying again on the upside, they said.
COPPER
A close at the day's high on Thursday suggested copper was poised for a further upward move aimed at taking out resistance at $2,366 -- assuming it eroded the interim bump at $2,340.
Getting beyond those two points would open the way to a test of trendline resistance at $2,410.
Confidence grew steadily in the market on Thursday after a weak start that reflected the previous bearish close.
But a below-forecast stock increase changed the mood and gave buying added momentum.
"Whether or not yesteday's lower stock build will become the trend remains to be seen. If it does then we might see come short covering," one analyst said.
Although copper could test further highs in the short term, rallies were still being viewed as forward selling opportunities.

And the close was not absolutely positive. "Technically despite (Thursday's) modest rally prices still closed bearishly and below the important 10-day moving average at $2,321 thus renewed downside pressure is likely," according to Bradeis (Brokers) Ltd's daily review.
Under that scenario, the $2,320 support came into question, followed by $2,285 and $2,270.
At 0700 GMT, copper was indicated at $2,333/$2,338, barely easier than London's late close.
ALUMINIUM
Consolidation looked in order for aluminium, which closed higher yesterday to continue the uptrend since its breakout on July 23.
"This market looks to be consolidating before breaking higher," said Harry Creates, technical analyst at Amalgamated Metal Trading.
The first resistance was immediately overhead at $1,712, which would signal $1,725 and $1,750 if broken, he added.
Below that, $1,677 support was needed to prevent a fall to $1,666 and $1,653.
"An interesting feature on the weekly chart is a reverse head and shoulders pattern which indicates that prices could eventually target $2,000," according to Bradeis (Brokers) Ltd's daily review.
"In the shorter term a close above $1,710 would have been more positive and the market continues to look slightly overbought," the review said.
At 0710 GMT aluminium was indicated at $1,710/$1,713, a shade below the late London level.
--Brian Spoors, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8058
